newsitem.title: USA: US Plains feedlot cattle bid $64, passed- feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains feedlot cattle bid $64, passed- feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Wednesday were quiet, with bids at $64.00 per cwt passed by owners who were generally pricing cattle at $66.00 to $67.00, feedlot sources said.
Fed cattle this week were expected to trade steady with last week's price of $65.00, but could turn lower if beef prices continue to erode, sources said.
Beef prices Tuesday were quoted down $0.42 to $1.52 per cwt on 321 fabricated loads sold, USDA said. The lightweight choice price was quoted at $98.52, down $1.65 since Friday.

There even was talk that several packers were considering pulling bids back to $63.00 in an attempt to maintain profitable operating margins following Tuesday's decline in beef prices, the sources said.
Feedlot cattle price weakness also could be generated by carryover selling following light sales Tuesday at $64.00 in Kansas on about 200 head that will likely grade mostly select, they said.
The falling beef prices were offsetting earlier optimism for firm fed cattle prices this week that were inspired by ideas packers were short of live cattle supplies, they said.
